cited.quote: Tamil Nadu Green Climate Fund has been established to develop projects in four key areas

rationale: C2 describes the Green Climate Fund covering energy transition, mobility, circular economy and water security, so not exclusively renewables. No guideline restricting spending to renewable energy and green investment appears in any extract.

cited.quote: Under this scheme, a subsidy of up to Rs.1 lakh will be provided to domestic consumers

rationale: C3 is a budget speech announcing a future rooftop solar scheme; C1 describes TNGECL aims. No renewable project is shown launched or funded from the climate fund. Only budget and policy-note statements.

cited.quote: TNESSF is a SEBI-registered Category-I Venture Capital Fund with a corpus of Rs.500 crore

rationale: C3 shows an existing TNESSF fund with Rs.500 crore corpus, apparently set up before this government and not dated after it took office. No new fund or official step for AI, deep-tech and FinTech start-ups is shown.

cited.quote: receive free nutritious meals, continuous medical monitoring and skilled obstetric care for 7 days

rationale: C3 reports Birth Waiting Rooms in tribal PHCs, benefiting mothers till March 2026, which predates this government and is limited to tribal areas. No dated new official step is shown for the promised centres.

cited.quote: identifies Tamils facing distress abroad to provide them with adequate assistance

rationale: C1 and C2 describe NRT welfare, helpline and legal aid, but none concerns property problems or a six-month resolution guideline. C3 is about financial fraud policing. No official step for this commitment.

cited.quote: Legal Assistance Center was established through the Commissionerate of Rehabilitation and Welfare

rationale: C2 shows a legal aid cell and helpline for NRTs, not a mechanism or tribunal disposing of property cases within a timeframe. C4 is a building appeal portal unrelated to NRTs. No relevant official step.

cited.quote: Hub-II: Seaweed Processing Park at Gandarvakottai, Pudukkottai District.

rationale: C1 shows a sanctioned seaweed park whose processing hub is in Pudukkottai, not Rameswaram; the Ramanathapuram hub is seed production. Sanction is undated. A different location does not fulfil the promise.

cited.quote: Non-Resident Tamil Investment Facilitation Desk and web portal 10 have been established under Guidance
Non-Resident Tamil Investment Promotion Division was established under Guidance Tamil Nadu as a single point of contact

rationale: C1 and C2 report the CM's letter to the diaspora and an NRT investment division, desk and portal established under Guidance (the budget speech C3 said the desk would be set up). Exact date not given, only the 2026 policy note.

cited.quote: drives formalization, credit access, and market expansion through targeted policy measures and digital ecosystems

rationale: C1 to C3 describe existing MSME schemes (NEEDS, TIIC loans, Udyam) with no new revival package or policy announced. C4 and C5 are health insurance orders. No dedicated revival step shown.

cited.quote: The Government of Tamil Nadu sets annual credit targets for MSMEs under the Annual Credit Plan.

rationale: Extracts show routine MSME credit schemes and annual credit plan, not an allocation of Rs.15000 crore of state funds for crisis-hit MSMEs. C5 is an unrelated health grant order.

cited.quote: are subsequently utilized for VIP bandobust duties, Personnel Security Officer and other VIP related duties

rationale: C1 shows women police personnel still being used for VIP bandobust duties; no order stopping this is shown. C2 and C3 are about women police contribution and welfare; C4 and C5 concern an anti-narcotics force.
No extract concerns an award or Rs.50 thousand cash prize for honest drivers. Extracts cover film, Tamil competition, women and disabled awards only.

cited.quote: The Scheme aims to provide concessional credit facilities through Scheduled Commercial Banks

rationale: C4 shows the Weaver Mudra credit scheme from 2016-17; C3 shows PMFME formalisation for food processing only. No step formalising handloom weaving micro and small enterprises is shown.

cited.quote: Initial administrative approval of Rs.17.21 crore has been accorded

rationale: C4 reports the AVGC-XR policy launched 13 March 2026, before the government took office, and a Viyan AVGC-XR hub being established with initial administrative approval accorded (undated, not yet operational). Treated as a preparatory official step.

cited.quote: including artificial intelligence, semiconductors and advanced electronics, aerospace and defence, Space technology, deep- tech and drone manufacturing, creative economy

rationale: C1 says the forthcoming Industrial Policy will emphasise creative economy; C2 says the policy is being finalised. These are only policy-note plans, not a new dedicated measure.

cited.quote: a Mango Technology Centre at Paiyur, Krishnagiri district, Chilli Technology Centres at Ramanathapuram

rationale: C5 only announces a future Mango Technology Centre in Krishnagiri, a different object from five integrated mango processing parks. C2 lists an existing food park in Dharmapuri. No official step for the promised parks.

cited.quote: covering the State's economic performance over the last five years

rationale: C2 reports an Economic Survey covering the last five years, not a decade-long growth report, and no new report of that kind. C5 is a revenue committee GO, not a growth report.

cited.quote: dedicated Industries Transformation Maps will be prepared for each of them

rationale: C5 says the new Industrial Policy is being formulated through consultation and maps will be prepared in future. No published policy document detailing industrial growth milestones is shown.

cited.quote: The Department implements several pioneering welfare schemes towards ensuring security, economic self-sufficiency

rationale: The promise is vague about the division. C1 and C2 describe the existing Social Welfare Department schemes for women and girls; no new step bringing them under a monitoring or regulating division is shown.

cited.quote: 84 Primary Processing Centres have been established across 20 districts

rationale: C1 lists existing general primary processing centres including three in Tenkasi, not a new centre for cardamom and spices for international marketing. C2 has no Tenkasi step. No relevant official step.
